prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1117; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a side-impact collision at an intersection in League City, Texas. Driver 1 was proceeding through the intersection when Driver 2 entered from a crossing street and struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. A Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact, and both the Passenger and Driver 1 were present on scene when officers arrived. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated by responding medical personnel. The injury Driver 1 described is consistent with the forces typical of a side impact of this kind. Driver 2 gave a statement that matched Driver 1's account of how the collision occurred. Two independent witnesses described the same sequence of events, and scene photographs show damage concentrated along the driver's side, which is largely consistent with the reported impact. Some faint scratches elsewhere on Driver 1's vehicle appear older than this collision and were noted but not attributed to it. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
